What supports demand: the coin is classed ORGANIC with no airdrop dump seen, it is still alive at 30.6 minutes, it drew 392 buyers, and the top-3 holder share (7.6%) and top-5 buyer share (23%) are not extreme. Buy volume in the last 15 minutes was 36.9 SOL from 108 buyers, so some participants are still arriving.

What works against it, and I think outweighs this: the last 15 minutes show net outflow of -6.8 SOL and a -23.6% return. Sell-to-buy ratio at graduation was about 1.0, meaning early buyers were distributing as fast as they bought. The coin is down 63% from its 30-minute high and down 53% over 30 minutes. The bundle share (15%) and completer share (15%) are meaningful, and the pool is shallow at 54 SOL, so our $20 ticket would face real slippage on both legs. The name "Dead Internet Theory" and the metadata host are data, not signal, and I can't read intent from them.

My verdict: there is no solid case for buying now. Demand exists but is leaving, and the trend is down. Skip.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is a slow bleed from distribution, not a single rug. The coin is already down 63% from its 30-minute high and 53% over 30 minutes, and in the last 15 minutes sellers (99) outnumbered buyers (108) with net outflow of -6.84 SOL and sell volume of 43.69 SOL against 36.85 SOL bought. The first two minutes after graduation show a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.002, meaning early buyers were already exiting at parity. Pool depth is only 54.47 SOL, so a $20 ticket plus the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost needs a clean bounce just to break even, and a dead-volume tape gives no reason to expect one. Decision: skip.
